author: AirFrameXR project (first profile; the knobs are the author's, tuned by A/B testing on stock ALVR + SteamVR)

fov.note: 0.8 client slider recommended (manually): set FoV Scale to 0.8 in the visionOS app, a value circulating in the community, then reconnect once; the stream then covers less angle and every pixel in view is about 1.25 times denser. The values here are the same with it at 1.0 or 0.8. Measured with the FoV grid (docs/AVP_FOV.md): left eye only, one person, one fit, the stock visionOS app (RealityKit) at its default FoV scale. The headset declares 106 x 96 degrees and shows about 80 x 74. Not yet tried in a game; check the corners for black with fovgrid.exe.

variants.label: Wi-Fi 6/6E, 5 or 6 GHz, strong signal, headset on the same subnet as the PC (the author's link; 300 Mbps measured stable with foveated encoding)

notes: Foveated encoding (ALVR's, centre 0.45 x 0.4, shift 0.4 / 0.1, edge ratio 4 x 5) is the recommended mode: measured on an RTX 5090 + Vision Pro at 100 Hz, encode 3.1 ms against 7.7 ms for the full 7104x3200 frame (spikes 14 ms against 18-33), headset decode about 1.5 ms lighter, NVENC under 10% against 54%, and 3x the bits per pixel at the same bitrate (0.39 against 0.12). The full frame showed no visible gain: the centre is native resolution in both modes and gets a third of the bits in full-frame mode.
Full frame (encode profile `full-split`) stays available for GPUs with 3 NVENC engines; it needs roughly 3x the bitrate to match the foveated centre quality, which Wi-Fi cannot carry.
The headset displays at 100 Hz while the stream is 90 fps: the host follows the headset's display rate.
Split encoding needs a GPU with several NVENC engines (RTX 4070 Ti and up, RTX 50 series).

session_overrides are ALVR session settings (dotted paths into config\\session.json): QuestPro emulation, NVENC preset P3 without multi-pass, CABAC, 10-bit HEVC, buffering 1.5 frames, no microphone, the Vision Pro's low-latency VideoToolbox option, chroma-key passthrough (optional, off by default; key colour #00FF00).

verified.result: 100 fps rendered and streamed in Cyberpunk 2077, total latency about 117 ms (ALVR's measure), 0 packets lost

Foveated 4224x1664 at 100 Hz in Cyberpunk 2077: host encode 3.1 ms, headset decode 5.4 ms, total latency about 117 ms; full frame in the same session: encode 7.7 ms, decode 6.8 ms, no visible quality gain
